executive_summary: CAD/JPY trades at 112.96588 as of the 2026-09-03 price-store close, meaning one Canadian dollar buys 112.97 yen; a rising pair is a stronger CAD against the yen. The pair is +0.32% over one month, −1.59% over three months, −3.45% over six months and +5.98% over twelve, and sits at the 64th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 105.418–117.245 — mid-upper on a one-year view but 251 pips below its 21 August high after two violent sessions on 2 and 3 September. The dominant bilateral narrative is a carry cross being dismantled from the quote leg: the bilateral policy differential is only +125bp (BoC 2.25% versus BoJ 1.00%), the joint-narrowest positive spread available against the yen in the G10, and the single scheduled policy decision inside the tactical window belongs to Japan, where the yen jumped more than 2% against the dollar on Thursday as traders unwound yen-funded carry trades, after Governor Ueda and board member Takata both raised the prospect of a larger-than-usual increase at the 18 September meeting. What diverges most from the standalone dossiers is the compensation arithmetic: this pair carries roughly USD/JPY-like volatility — a 7.437% three-month ATM estimate against 7.85% sixty-day realised — on a third of USD/JPY's carry, giving a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.17 and a six-month carry cushion of 70 pips, exactly one day's ATR(14). The offsetting bilateral fact, and the reason the pair is not more bearish, is that crude moves both legs the same way for CAD/JPY: Brent's 20-day range is US$92.3–97.0, with escalation in Kuwait testing above US$97 and confirmed calm testing below US$92, and every dollar of that is revenue to the base economy and cost to the quote economy. The settled stance is Bearish on both horizons — tactical conviction 2 at a net score of −0.1027, strategic conviction 3 at −0.1855 — and the caveat is that the tactical score clears the Neutral boundary by 0.0027 while the price payload shows a large slice of the September repricing has already been delivered, so the direction is right and the entry is late.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no pair-level PPP series for CAD/JPY and none is asserted. On BIS real effective exchange rates the two legs sit at 95.71 (CAD, June 2026) and 65.3 (JPY, June 2026), a 30.4-point gap that makes the quote currency roughly 31.8% cheap against the base currency on a relative real basis — a mechanical scaling of the two REER indices against their common 2020 base, not a fair-value estimate. The quote currency is the cheapest major currency in the world on that measure and has been for three years, which means valuation is a magnitude constraint on the bull case for this pair rather than a timing signal: it caps how far CAD/JPY can extend, without telling you when. What is priced into 112.97 is a persistent policy differential rather than any real-exchange-rate mean reversion, and the forward curve is discounting the pair by only 1.18% annualised, which is the differential expressed as a price and nothing more.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime for this cross over the visible window is one of official flow repeatedly resetting a carry trade that keeps re-forming, and then failing to hold. The 52-week high of 117.49155 was printed intraday on 30 April in a session that closed 217 pips lower at 115.32536 — the day of the largest single-day yen-buying operation in the Ministry of Finance series. The pair then chopped between roughly 113.50 and 116.50 for three months before collapsing on 30-31 July, when a 116.35 open became a 112.35 close in two sessions, bottoming at 110.76762 intraday on 3 August after the joint US-Japan intervention. Through August it clawed almost all of that back, closing at 115.48468 on 21 August and 115.29739 on 31 August, which is the empirical evidence that official flow alone does not change this pair's regime. That reset ended abruptly: 2 September closed at 114.64753 and 3 September at 112.96588 on a 227-pip range, a two-session decline of 2.0% that took the pair below all three of its medium-term averages and within 220 pips of the 3 August low. This time the driver is policy expectation rather than official flow, which is the distinction that matters for whether it holds.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: 125bp on 112.96588 is 1.412 yen a year. Over four weeks that is 11 pips; over six months, 70 pips. Against an ATR(14) of 70 pips, four weeks of carry is 0.15 of a single average day's range, and six months of carry is exactly one average day. A 227-pip session, as delivered on 3 September, wipes out more than three years of accrued differential.
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral policy differential is +125bp: Bank of Canada at 2.25% against Bank of Japan at 1.00% — the joint-narrowest positive spread available against the yen in the G10, level with EUR, and against AUD's 335bp, USD's 262.5bp and GBP's 275bp. The market-observable cost of rolling the position is the payload's futures premium of −117.7bp annualised, roughly 7bp inside the policy differential; by covered interest parity that figure is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and the two cannot be separated without an OIS curve. The sign is positive and the compensation is the worst in the positive-carry yen complex: CAD/JPY runs 60-day realised volatility of 7.85%, marginally above USD/JPY's 7.51%, while paying 125bp against USD/JPY's 262.5bp. Carry therefore neither funds nor meaningfully offsets a directional view at the tactical horizon, and only becomes material at six months, where it is worth 0.63%. The practical consequence cuts in the direction of the settled stance: a bearish CAD/JPY position costs 11 pips to hold for four weeks and 70 pips for six months, which is a fraction of what the same view costs expressed through AUD/JPY or NOK/JPY. Being wrong here is cheap; being right is not subsidised.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is +125bp in the base currency's favour: Bank of Canada 2.25 per cent against Bank of Japan 1.00 per cent. The level supports CAD/JPY; the direction of travel does not, and inside the tactical window the direction is all that is dated. The scheduled-decisions file contains exactly one decision in the next four weeks and it belongs to the quote currency: the Bank of Japan on 2026-09-18. The Bank of Canada's next fixed announcement date is 2026-10-28, outside the tactical horizon, and the 2026-09-02 decision has already been delivered as a hold at 2.25 per cent for a seventh consecutive meeting. So the arithmetic is one-sided by construction: the differential can only narrow from 125bp toward 100bp inside four weeks, and cannot widen at all through policy action. Sovereign spreads corroborate the same direction. The gated payload gives CAD 10-year 3.42 per cent against JPY 2.67 per cent for a +75bp gap, both legs monthly as of 2026-06-01 and therefore not live; on the dossiers' live prints of roughly 3.74 per cent and 2.94 per cent the gap is near +79bp and the Japanese leg has since touched 3.00 per cent, compressing it further. Transmission is direct: CAD/JPY is a carry cross whose entire fundamental support is the differential, and every basis point of compression removes that support. The carry itself is thin, which is the neglected bilateral fact: 125bp is the joint-narrowest positive spread available against the yen in the G10, level with EUR and far below AUD at 335bp or USD at 262.5bp, so the cushion protecting a long CAD/JPY position is roughly a third of what an AUD/JPY holder enjoys against very similar volatility.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two policy paths point in opposite directions and neither is speculative. The strategic window contains four dated decisions from the gated file: Bank of Canada on 2026-10-28 with a Monetary Policy Report, Bank of Japan on 2026-10-30 with an Outlook Report, then Bank of Canada on 2026-12-09 and Bank of Japan on 2026-12-18. On the Canadian side the consensus after the September hold is no change, with TD explicitly expecting rates unchanged through next year and the base dossier reading the residual market-implied 2026 hike probability as a mispricing to be faded at the October MPR. On the Japanese side MUFG's published path is 1.25 per cent in September 2026, 1.50 per cent in January 2027 and 1.75 per cent by June 2027, and half of the surveyed economist panel now names 1.75 per cent as terminal. Take the September and December BoJ meetings alone and the differential goes from +125bp to +75bp with the Canadian leg static; on the full published path it reaches +50bp by mid-2027. There is no credible six-month scenario in which the differential widens, and only a narrow one in which it holds. The transmission for CAD/JPY is unusually pure because neither currency's rate story runs through the other: the compression is delivered entirely by the quote leg, so it does not depend on any judgement about Canada at all. The offsetting consideration, which caps confidence, is that a differential can compress without spot following — the quote dossier documents exactly that failure over the past year — and part of the Japanese yield rise is a fiscal risk premium rather than a policy signal, which is scored separately in Factor 8.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth and inflation differentials point in opposite directions over four weeks and the honest reading is a standoff. On growth the base currency wins clearly: Canada printed 3.3 per cent annualised in Q2 against Japan's 0.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter, or 1.1 per cent annualised, and Canadian unemployment fell to a two-year low of 6.4 per cent while the August data ledger ran five beats to three misses. On inflation the quote currency wins on the measure that matters for policy: Canadian headline is 3.0 per cent but the Bank of Canada's own core measures average exactly 2.0 per cent with the entire headline-core gap attributable to gasoline, and the Bank's 2026-09-02 statement noted little evidence of energy prices spreading to other components. Japanese core is 1.8 per cent and rising, the Bank of Japan's ex-special-factors measure is 2.3 per cent, Tokyo core has accelerated three consecutive months, and the energy-subsidy unwind is arithmetic rather than forecast. The transmission asymmetry is what makes this Neutral rather than directional: strong Canadian activity data no longer moves the Canadian front end much because the Bank has told the market it is looking through oil and is comfortable holding, whereas a Japanese core print at or above 2.0 per cent on 2026-09-17 feeds directly into a decision the following day. Two Canadian releases and one Japanese release fall inside the window and the Japanese one has the shorter fuse.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the growth differential that favours the base currency reverses and the inflation differential that favours the quote currency persists, so both channels turn against the pair. Canada's July advance GDP estimate was 0.0 per cent and that reading predates both the 50 per cent Section 338 duties of 2026-08-22 and the Canadian counter-measures of 2026-09-08; the Bank of Canada's own July projection of 0.7 per cent for 2026 as a whole implies materially sub-trend Canadian outcomes in the second half after a 3.3 per cent annualised Q2. On the Japanese side the Bank of Japan's Outlook has core CPI at 2.5 per cent in FY2026 and 2.4 per cent in FY2027, the FY2027 figure revised up, with the FY2026 cut explicitly attributed to temporary energy subsidies whose unwind is already scheduled. So the relative inflation picture over the horizon is Canadian headline converging down toward a 2.0 per cent core as gasoline base effects roll off, against Japanese core converging up through 2 per cent as subsidies lapse — a two-sided move in the same direction for the pair. Business-cycle position reinforces it: Canada is entering a tariff-induced slowdown with 6.4 per cent unemployment and 2.8 per cent wage growth decelerating, while Japan is running a 2.4 per cent unemployment rate with a third consecutive shunto above 5 per cent and six straight months of positive real wages. The offset is that Japanese domestic demand is weak — private consumption contributed nothing to Q2 — which is why confidence is 58 rather than higher.

The mechanical inflection is the arrival of post-tariff Canadian activity data — the October monthly GDP release covering August, then the Q3 national accounts — alongside the 2026-10-30 Outlook Report on the Japanese side.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: CAD/JPY is a moderate-beta risk cross rather than a pure one, and the current cross-asset configuration supports it. VIX closed at 14.51 near the 2026 low of 14.13, US investment-grade option-adjusted spreads are 79bp and high-yield 263bp after tightening 21bp on the month, the S&P 500 is up 13-16 per cent year to date and the Nikkei is up 58.4 per cent over twelve months. That is the environment in which a funding currency bleeds and a mildly pro-cyclical commodity currency holds, and the classification is consistent across both dossiers: the base currency carries a modest positive risk beta anchored by its US economic linkage, roughly half the Antipodean sensitivity, while the quote currency has the strongest negative VIX correlation in the G10. The bilateral beta is therefore positive but moderate — lower than AUD/JPY or NZD/JPY, which is why this cross is not the instrument of choice for expressing a risk view in either direction. Two complications temper the stance. First, the current oil strength is supply-driven rather than demand-driven, which severs the channel through which the base currency's risk beta was historically earned: crude is rising because of Persian Gulf disruption, not because global growth is accelerating. Second, Canadian equities have underperformed the global complex on tariff exposure, so the domestic risk proxy is not confirming the global one. The level of risk appetite is supportive; its composition is not clean.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel delivers no directional signal for this pair and Neutral is a considered conclusion rather than a default. The modal path is persistence: if VIX stays near 14 and credit stays at 79bp, the funding leg keeps bleeding and the pair grinds higher on carry, which is the single most likely six-month outcome and the reason the stance is not Bearish. Against that sits an unusually well-identified tail. A volatility regime break hits CAD/JPY through both legs simultaneously — the quote currency gains on safe-haven and repatriation flow while the base currency loses on its pro-cyclical beta and on a commodity complex that would fall with global demand — so the pair's downside convexity in a risk event is materially larger than its upside convexity in a continued melt-up. The August 2024 analogue and the identified 2026 pressure points, including the US appropriations deadline and the midterm elections, are the mechanism. The bilateral netting of the commodity channel completes the offset: a demand-driven risk-off would take crude lower, which removes the base currency's terms-of-trade support at the same moment the quote currency gains a haven bid, whereas a supply-driven crude spike helps the base currency but suppresses the global growth its exports serve. Neither tail is directionally clean, and the modal path and the tail point opposite ways with roughly comparable expected value.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Speculators are net short both legs, which mutes the pair signal relative to either dossier read in isolation, but the marginal flows run in opposite directions and that is where the bilateral signal lives. On the base leg, combined leveraged-fund and asset-manager positioning was net short 131,035 contracts at the 2026-08-25 reference date after 65,515 contracts of covering in a fortnight, with open interest down 8.4 per cent — liquidation, not accumulation, and roughly a third of the fuel already burned. On the quote leg, leveraged funds were net short 77,042 contracts and had been ADDING for three consecutive weeks, 23,972 contracts of fresh gross shorts into a shrinking open-interest base. Since then that has reversed hard: a rush to unwind yen-funded carry positions has been reported into the September BoJ meeting, following hawkish comments from the Governor and from a board member raising the possibility of an outsized increase. That is the specific flow this cross is most exposed to, because CAD/JPY is a carry vehicle whose bid comes from the same books. Netting the two: base-leg short covering is a tailwind for the pair, quote-leg short covering is a headwind, and the quote-leg unwind is the one with fresh momentum, larger notional at the margin and a dated catalyst on 2026-09-18. Structural flow reinforces the bearish side — Japanese residents sold a net JPY 1,978.4bn of foreign bonds in a single August week and life-insurer hedge ratios sit at historic lows.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: On a one-to-six-month view the stock rather than the flow decides it, and the stocks are asymmetric in the pair's disfavour. The base leg carries a residual speculative short of 131,035 contracts against dealers long 124,930, which is a genuine cushion under the base currency and the strongest positioning argument for the pair — but it is a cushion, not a catalyst, and positioning has never been a six-month driver on its own. The quote leg carries something larger and invisible in futures data: Japanese life-insurer currency hedge ratios at historically low levels, confirmed independently by a Daiwa survey of ten major insurers and a Bank of Japan Review, where normalisation is simultaneously spot yen buying and a widening of the short-dated basis. That normalisation is triggered by exactly the base case in Factor 1 — a rising Japanese policy rate lowering the relative attraction of unhedged foreign assets — so it is a consequence of the central scenario rather than a shock. Add the pension rebalancing channel, with GPIF holding foreign equities at 25.33 per cent against a 25 per cent target after a strongly positive quarter, and the structural bid for the quote currency is both larger and more mechanically triggered than the residual short-covering bid for the base currency. Confidence is held at 55 because the timing of hedge-ratio normalisation is genuinely unknowable and because reserve managers cut the yen's allocated COFER share by 0.40 percentage points in a single quarter, which is a real structural offset.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with confidence easing from 58 to 55. The tactical case is flow: a reported yen-short unwind with a dated catalyst against a base-currency covering wave that is already a third spent. The strategic case is stock: a mechanically triggered life-insurer hedging channel on the quote leg against a residual speculative short on the base leg that is a cushion without a trigger. Flow is tradeable over weeks; stock only pays over months if something arrives to set it off, and here the trigger is the Factor 1 base case itself.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Positioning is NOT stretched: 77,042 contracts of leveraged-fund short at the 33rd percentile with a z-score of −0.56 is roughly half the 2026 extreme of 115,400 and barely a third of the −150,000 the currency brief identifies as historically extreme. There is no squeeze setup here.
tactical.unwind_trigger: A 17 September core CPI print at or above 2.0% followed by an 18 September hike accompanied by explicit language on accelerating the pace, against a Federal Reserve that holds rather than hikes on 16 September.
tactical.historical_analogue: The same funds are short 143,570 gross USD/JPY contracts and the options market is already paying 1.74 volatility points for the outcome, which could produce a 400-600 pip USD/JPY move toward the 155.20 post-intervention low if the sequence above fires.
tactical.contrarian_case: What could nonetheless trigger a violent unwind inside four weeks is not the size of the position but its concentration: leveraged funds hold 37.4 per cent of total open interest on the short side against dealers at 14.8 per cent, and open interest is 26 per cent below its June peak, so the book is narrow. That sequence would reprice the differential from both ends in 48 hours. The contrarian case against our own tactical stance is that the market has now watched the yen fail to hold gains after a record intervention, a BoJ hike and a 30-year high in Japanese yields, and has correctly concluded that yen rallies are for selling; on that view the right response to any dip is to add short yen. Positioning today is genuinely a neutral signal — the shorts are neither crowded enough to squeeze nor light enough to imply capitulation.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: 131,035 contracts of base-currency speculative short set against the quote leg's structural latent buyer — Japanese life-insurer hedge ratios at record lows and Japanese retail net long foreign currency 2.05:1 — raises the question of whether the base-leg short represents exhaustion or conviction.
strategic.unwind_trigger: Japanese policy reaching 1.50 per cent, the point at which insurers have said they would raise hedge ratios; on the base side, confirmation of the 2027-01-01 tariff escalation would deepen rather than relieve the speculative short.
strategic.historical_analogue: The base-currency speculative short reached comparable extremes in the early-2025 tariff cycle and took roughly five months to normalise, trading a wide range rather than trending, which argues the base-leg cushion supports the pair without driving it.
strategic.contrarian_case: The evidence favours exhaustion on the base-leg flow and a latent buyer on the quote leg: Japanese life-insurer hedge ratios are at record lows, Japanese retail is net long foreign currency 2.05:1, and a record C$80.8bn of foreign purchases of Canadian government bonds is a completed allocation already in the price rather than a forward flow. The strongest contrarian argument against a six-month bearish pair view is that the quote currency has now failed to rally through a record intervention, a policy hike, a multi-decade high in its own long yields and a narrowing differential. Four yen-positive impulses produced net depreciation. If that pattern holds, the residual base-currency short covers, carry accrues, and the pair grinds higher regardless of what the two central banks do.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised +0.04 tactically and +0.03 strategically. This is the single cleanest bilateral factor on the board: a net energy exporter with the entire energy complex carved out of its tariff regime against an economy that imports essentially all of its hydrocarbons, with an active Persian Gulf supply disruption running through both legs in the same direction for the pair. The default weights understate a channel in which one commodity moves both currencies the same way for CAD/JPY.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the pair's strongest bullish factor and the mechanism is unusually direct. The base economy posted a Q2 current account surplus of C$8.8bn, the first since 2022 and the largest since 2005, on record energy and auto exports, against a consensus of C$3.5bn; the quote economy posted a July trade deficit of JPY 638.3bn, 4.1 times wider year on year, with mineral fuels at 22.1 per cent of all imports and up 53.5 per cent, and produced its first monthly current-account deficit in seventeen months in June. The quote economy's terms of trade have collapsed from 90.5 in Q1 2026 to 81.62 in July while the base economy's have improved, and the driver is the same variable for both: crude between roughly US$90 and US$93 with JKM LNG up 101.9 per cent year on year. Applying the direction rules, oil higher is strongly positive for the base currency and strongly negative for the quote currency, and LNG higher is strongly negative for the quote currency alone — so a single commodity move pushes both legs the same way for the pair, which is true of almost no other G10 cross except NOK/JPY. The tariff carve-out is decisive here: energy, potash, fish and critical minerals were excluded from the Section 338 duties, so the base economy's largest export category trades on global prices rather than bilateral politics. Bilateral trade itself is a modest offset: IMF DOTS shows the base economy exporting US$10.9bn of goods to the quote economy against US$16.2bn of imports for a net balance of minus US$5.2bn, so the direct trade relationship runs against the base currency even as the global commodity channel runs for it.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.19 strategic weight this is the largest single positive contribution in either horizon, and the case strengthens as the measurement window lengthens. The EIA expects Brent to average roughly US$87 for 2026 with approximately 0.6 million barrels per day of Strait of Hormuz disruption persisting through the end of 2027, which is a multi-quarter, supply-side transfer of income from importers to non-Gulf producers. The base economy is a direct beneficiary whose commodity complex is exempt from the bilateral tariff regime; the quote economy is a direct payer with no offsetting production. The quote economy's headline external position is still a large surplus — a record first-half current account of JPY 17.43trn — but the composition is the point: primary income is 27.6 times the goods surplus, and investment income is largely reinvested offshore rather than converted, whereas it is the goods account that generates spot flow, and the goods account has turned negative and is deteriorating. Two structural markers point the same way: the quote economy slipped to third-largest net creditor in the world and its net position actually fell to JPY 560.1trn at end-March 2026 while gross assets rose. The base economy's current account, at minus 0.87 per cent of GDP in Q1 and positive in Q2, now compares favourably with every deficit country in the benchmarking set. The offsets that cap confidence at 65 are real: 70 per cent of base-economy exports still go to one increasingly hostile customer, the heavy-oil differential caps realisation of any Brent rally, and a Hormuz reopening would reverse the entire mechanism in weeks.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish on both horizons with confidence rising from 60 to 65 and the applied weight rising from 0.10 to 0.19. That is deliberate: the tactical read depends on two monthly trade prints, while the strategic read rests on a supply-side energy regime the EIA expects to persist into 2028, a quarterly external surplus on the base leg and a terms-of-trade deterioration on the quote leg that compounds every month it continues.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Net energy exporter. Crude oil is the dominant export, supported by natural gas, potash, aluminium, uranium and lumber. Oil higher is strongly positive for the base currency, and critically the entire energy and critical-minerals complex was carved out of the 50 per cent Section 338 duties, so it trades on global prices rather than bilateral politics.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Pure commodity importer with essentially no domestic hydrocarbon production. Mineral fuels were 22.1 per cent of July imports and rose 53.5 per cent year on year on FALLING volumes, so the entire increase is price. Oil higher is strongly negative; JKM LNG higher, up 101.9 per cent year on year, is strongly negative; thermal coal higher is negative.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: base currency ++, quote currency −−. Both signs push CAD/JPY the same way, so the pair rises on a magnitude close to the sum of the two effects rather than a netted difference. LNG up: base currency neutral-to-mildly-positive as a nascent exporter, quote currency −−, so the pair rises again. This double-sided alignment is the defining structural feature of this cross and it is shared in the G10 only with NOK/JPY. It also cuts the other way with equal force: oil down transmits a negative to the base leg and a positive to the quote leg simultaneously, so the pair's commodity beta is roughly twice what either currency's standalone exposure suggests. The measurable evidence is that the quote economy's terms of trade fell from 90.5 to 81.62 in two quarters while the base economy swung to its largest current-account surplus in twenty-one years, in the same two quarters, driven by the same crude move.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent 10 per cent higher, from roughly US$91 toward US$100, is materially bullish CAD/JPY. The base economy's energy export revenue rises with the tariff carve-out intact and the current-account surplus extends; the quote economy's monthly trade deficit widens toward or beyond JPY 900bn, its terms-of-trade index falls below 78 and consecutive current-account deficits become the base case. This is the strongest single bullish scenario available to this cross, and on the price payload it maps to a recovery through the four-touch 113.867–114.560 band toward the five-touch zone at 115.469–116.413.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent 10 per cent lower, toward US$82, is materially bearish CAD/JPY and would be the cleanest invalidator of the pair's bullish offset. The base economy loses its terms-of-trade support at the same moment tariff drag shows up in Q4 activity, and its headline CPI converges down toward the 2.0 per cent core average, removing the statistical basis for any hike premium; the quote economy's terms of trade recover, its trade deficit narrows and the heaviest bearish contribution to its own dossier disappears. On the payload this is the path that carries the pair through the thin three-touch floor at 111.410–112.164 to the nine-touch band at 108.920–110.000.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Brent crude, with JKM LNG as the amplifier on the quote leg. A Strait of Hormuz reopening, or a sustained escalation, is the single most important non-policy variable for this pair over both horizons — more important than any equity index or credit spread. The current reference range is tight and the risk is live: Brent's 20-day range is US$92.3 to US$97.0, with escalation in Kuwait testing above US$97 and confirmed calm testing below US$92.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The guidance divergence between the two central banks is as wide as anything on this board, and the sequencing has just resolved in the quote currency's favour. The base-currency central bank delivered its decision on 2026-09-02, holding for a seventh consecutive meeting with what TD Economics described as an even-handed assessment and a comfortable holding pattern; the statement noted little evidence of higher energy prices spreading into other components while acknowledging that upside inflation risks have increased, which is language that commits to nothing and leaves the October Monetary Policy Report as the next informative communication. The quote-currency central bank is doing the opposite. Its July Summary of Opinions carried the formulation that the pace of rate increases will be faster than market expectations, its Governor said on 2026-09-01 that the Board would debate raising rates in September with a focus on whether inflation risks are heightening and that it hopes to keep raising rates while financial conditions remain accommodative, its Deputy Governor called for timely increases in late August, and a board member has since raised the possibility of an outsized move. Layered on top is an asymmetry with no counterpart on the base leg: the US Treasury Secretary has publicly met the Governor and called for decisive steps against yen weakness. One central bank is pre-committing to a direction; the other is pre-committing to optionality. For a pair whose only support is the differential, that transmits directly.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months guidance carries a 0.12 weight and is the second-heaviest bearish contributor. The two banks' reaction functions have moved in opposite directions in a way that is durable rather than tactical. The quote-currency Board reframed its objective from lifting inflation toward 2 per cent to stabilising it and preventing an upward deviation, which mechanically converts every upside inflation surprise into a tightening impulse, revised its FY2027 core forecast up while attributing the FY2026 cut to temporary energy subsidies, and abolished the scheduled interim assessment of its bond-purchase plan so that balance-sheet changes now happen ad hoc at meetings — raising the probability of an unscheduled hawkish surprise. The base-currency Board is doing the reverse: looking through oil, disclosing an internal range of views on the sustainability of the rebound, and preserving flexibility in both directions. The dated test is a pair of projection rounds two days apart. On 2026-10-28 the base-currency bank must publish a full forecast round incorporating post-tariff activity data, which the base dossier expects to mark growth down and remove the residual 2026 hike premium; on 2026-10-30 the quote-currency bank publishes an Outlook Report into a terms-of-trade shock and a scheduled subsidy unwind, with an upward skew to its inflation revision. Both projection rounds, on the analysis above, resolve against the pair. Credibility is the offset: the quote-currency bank has surprised in both directions historically and the FX market has sold its currency through an entire hiking cycle, which is why confidence is 66 rather than higher.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with confidence rising from 62 to 66 and the weight rising from 0.07 to 0.12. Tactically the guidance edge is confined to one press conference on the quote leg, because the base leg's decision has already passed and produced no signal. Strategically both banks must publish numbers within 48 hours of each other in late October, and a reaction function is far more predictable over a forecast round than a single meeting's tone.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both legs carry heavy dated event risk and the balance tips against the pair. On the base leg, retaliatory tariffs on approximately US$20bn of US goods at rates of 15-50 per cent take effect on 2026-09-08, and the product-level composition had not been published at the valuation date, so the market cannot have priced it; this follows the 2026-08-22 imposition of 50 per cent Section 338 duties with no expiry and no negotiating calendar, after talks collapsed. On the quote leg, the dominant event risk is official intervention and it only ever points one way: approximately JPY 27.1trn of yen buying in calendar 2026 against a previous full-year record of JPY 15.32trn, including a joint operation with the US Treasury, with the Finance Minister stating no hesitation about further joint action and the US Treasury Secretary repeating the commitment. That is a well-capitalised, publicly committed bid under the quote currency with no corresponding official seller, and no equivalent official support for the base currency. Running the other way is the Persian Gulf: continued escalation raises the base economy's export revenue and the quote economy's import bill simultaneously, which is bullish for the pair, and it is the single event channel that supports it. Netting the three, the two unpriced binaries with dates inside the window — Canadian retaliation on 2026-09-08 and an intervention-capable official sector on the quote leg — both push the pair lower, while the commodity channel pushes it higher with no date attached.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the base leg's event risk is a structural condition rather than a series of dates, and that is what makes it heavier than the quote leg's. Section 338 permits proclamation-only tariffs with no investigation, no hearing and no time limit, so there is no statutory clock forcing the parties back to the table; the base economy's own government expects no substantive talks before the November midterms and is designing industry support on the assumption it outlasts the current US administration. The escalation is already announced and dated: duties on base-economy cars, trucks, parts and steel rise to 50 per cent from 2027-01-01, and the USMCA architecture that would normally constrain this has been dismantled with the base economy absent from the parallel bilateral track. Against that, the quote leg's strategic event risk is genuinely two-sided — the intervention option persists but has a demonstrated half-life of under a month, while the energy channel accrues continuously against it, and the quote economy's own fiscal event risk is scored in Factor 8. The bilateral political relationship between the two economies is quiet and carries no direct risk premium; there is no trade dispute, no sanctions issue and a stable energy-supply relationship. So the strategic event asymmetry reduces to a permanent, escalating and unnegotiable tariff regime on the base leg against an ambiguous set of risks on the quote leg, and the only dated circuit-breaker inside the horizon is the 2026-11-03 US midterms, whose transmission is indirect and slow.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with confidence rising from 57 to 60. The tactical risk is the unpublished composition of a single retaliation list plus a live official bid under the quote currency — bounded uncertainties that resolve quickly. The strategic risk is the absence of any mechanism to end the base leg's tariff regime, compounded by a dated escalation on 2027-01-01. Duration, not magnitude, makes the longer horizon the stronger case.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised +0.01 strategically only. This is not a dormant relative-value comparison on this pair: the quote economy has a live fiscal risk premium visible in an inverted 25s30s segment, a record debt-service line at a raised assumed rate, and a documented mechanism by which its own central bank's tightening worsens its budget arithmetic — the specific reason its currency failed to rally through a multi-decade high in its own long yields. The default 0.07 understates a channel that is actively transmitting.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign differential is wide, unambiguous and currently active on the quote leg. The base economy is rated AAA by S&P, Aaa by Moody's and AAA by DBRS with AA+ from Fitch, one of only two AAA-rated G7 sovereigns, with an improving budget balance, a deficit revised down to C$66.9bn and record foreign demand for its government bonds at C$80.8bn in Q2. The quote economy is rated A1, A+ and A, carries general government gross debt of roughly 214.5 per cent of GDP on the IMF-style measure, and submitted FY2027 ministry budget requests of approximately JPY 143trn including a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line after raising its assumed interest rate to 3.8 per cent from 3.0 per cent. The transmission for this pair is the important part and it inverts the naive sign. Rising quote-economy yields would ordinarily support the quote currency through the differential, but a rise driven by a fiscal risk premium carries no currency-positive content, and the evidence that this is what is happening is specific: the quote economy's 25s30s segment is inverted, its 30s40s is flat, a recent 2-year auction drew a bid-to-cover well below its twelve-month average, and its currency did not rally as its 10-year touched 3.00 per cent for the first time since 1996. That is a directly bullish channel for CAD/JPY, and the more the quote-currency central bank tightens, the more the debt-service line grows — roughly JPY 5trn per 100bp — which is the self-limiting feature of the Factor 1 bearish case.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the fiscal differential is the pair's second-largest positive contribution and it compounds. On the base leg, federal debt-to-GDP is projected above 43 per cent by 2027-28 before stabilising, the lowest net position in the G7, financed comfortably by record foreign inflows in the same quarter the current account swung positive — the base economy is not required to depreciate its currency to clear its capital account. On the quote leg, the arithmetic runs the other way: an uncapped new investment category above JPY 10trn inside the FY2027 request, a stimulus package worth roughly 3.7 per cent of GDP, a widening deficit path on IMF projections, and a central bank that is stepping back from JGB purchases from JPY 2.5trn a month toward JPY 2.0trn by April 2027 precisely as supply rises. The single most important dated event for this factor is the FY2027 draft budget approval in late December: if new issuance breaches the stated cap, the fiscal channel dominates the policy channel on the quote leg and the pair's bearish thesis loses its largest engine. The offsets that hold confidence at 62 rather than higher are genuine on both sides — roughly 90 per cent of quote-economy government bonds are domestically held with three stable rating outlooks and no agency action in 2026, while the base economy's tariff support package is explicitly open-ended and unbudgeted against a shrinking tariff-exposed tax base.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish on both horizons with confidence rising from 58 to 62 and the applied weight from 0.04 to 0.08. Tactically the factor is expressed through auctions and budget headlines that are partly discounted. Strategically it is the compounding arithmetic of a debt-service line that rises roughly JPY 5trn per 100bp against a central bank expected to deliver 50-75bp inside the window while simultaneously reducing its bond purchases — supply rising as the dominant buyer withdraws.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This factor is the framework's sole price exemption, and in this pass the price series has been deliberately withheld, so the only structural input available is the pair's own volatility surface from the gated store. That surface is informative in one respect and silent in another. It is silent on direction: without trailing returns, moving averages, range percentiles or touch-counted zones there is no structural evidence for a stance, and manufacturing one from the two legs' separate charts would be exactly the laundering this pass exists to prevent. What it does say is that CAD/JPY carries volatility close to USD/JPY's while paying a third of USD/JPY's carry. The 3-month ATM estimate is 7.437 per cent at a 94.7-day tenor, with the term structure upward sloping from 7.025 per cent at 38.6 days to 7.743 per cent at 185.7 days, and the pair's 60-day realised volatility is 7.25 per cent — so implied sits marginally above realised on an estimate that is documented to run low by 9-18 per cent, meaning the true variance premium is probably negative at the front. Against 125bp of carry that gives a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.17 at best and closer to 0.15 on a corrected vol, the weakest of the positive-carry yen crosses. The structural conclusion is about compensation rather than direction: this pair pays poorly for the risk it carries, which argues against a spot expression in either direction and says nothing about which way it goes. On the second pass, the payload's own realised-volatility figures are 7.69% (20d) and 7.85% (60d), both marginally above the 7.25% sixty-day figure quoted from the quote dossier's cross table, which strengthens rather than weakens the compensation argument above; the payload also supplies the structural map (moving averages, touch-counted zones, ATR and range percentile) reproduced in the Pair Technicals section, none of which alters the Neutral stance recorded here.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the structural picture is even less informative and the weight falls to 0.03, so this factor should not move the synthesis and does not. Inflation and Growth is a Neutral at 0.18 tactical weight, contributing nothing, but becomes a Bearish at 0.10 strategic weight, contributing −0.058 — the base economy's pre-tariff data strength is a four-week fact and its post-tariff slowdown is a six-month one. Guidance nearly doubles from 0.07 to 0.12 as the horizon lengthens to include two projection rounds where both banks must publish numbers. Working the other way, Terms of Trade rises from 0.10 to 0.19, so the offsetting commodity channel also gets heavier — but not heavily enough to catch up.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Direction is the same on both horizons, so there is no inflection to manage — but the two calls do not deserve the same size. The tactical score sits 0.0027 beyond the Neutral boundary and one confidence point would flip it, and the price payload shows the move has already run 2.0% in two sessions into a support band, so tactical exposure should be minimal and event-driven around 2026-09-18. The strategic call is where the conviction sits, and the natural staging point is the pair of projection rounds on 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-30. The pair's thin 125bp carry means a bearish position costs 70 pips to hold for six months, a genuine and quantifiable advantage over expressing the identical view through AUD/JPY or NOK/JPY, where the same holding period costs 165-170 pips.

catalysts.event: Base-economy retaliatory tariffs take effect on approximately US$20bn of US goods at 15-50%
catalysts.rationale: The product-level composition was unpublished at the valuation date, so the market cannot have priced it. Retaliation is self-inflicted cost on an economy roughly one tenth the size of its counterparty, raising domestic prices while reducing choice, and it invites further US escalation. Transmission to the pair is through the base leg's growth outlook, which feeds directly into the differential that is the pair's only support.

catalysts.event: Quote-economy August corporate goods price index and terms-of-trade series
catalysts.rationale: The July reading had the terms-of-trade index at 81.62 from 90.5 in Q1, with yen-basis import prices up 29.1% against 17.7% in contract-currency terms. With crude in a US$92.3-97.0 range and JKM LNG up 101.9%, August should deteriorate further. This is the input to the single factor supporting the pair, and a worse print strengthens the bullish offset on the quote leg.

catalysts.event: Base-economy Consumer Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: The most important base-economy release in the tactical window. Headline sits at 3.0% entirely because of gasoline while the bank's core measures average exactly 2.0%. If CPI-trim rises toward 2.2% the oil-broadening risk the bank has said it would respond to becomes live and the base leg gains rate support, lifting the pair; if it slips, the residual hike premium that is the base currency's best remaining support starts to bleed out.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: Roughly 57-66% of a 25bp hike is priced. Neither leg of this cross is the dollar, so transmission is asymmetric rather than direct: the quote currency's differential to the dollar is 262.5bp against the base currency's 137.5bp, so a hawkish outcome hurts the quote leg roughly twice as much and lifts the pair. It also lands 48 hours before the quote-currency decision, so the two events partially net rather than compound.

catalysts.event: Quote-economy national Consumer Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: July printed 1.9% headline and 1.8% core, with the central bank's own ex-special-factors measure at 2.3% and government subsidies suppressing the headline by roughly 40-50bp. Tokyo core has accelerated three consecutive months and the rebasing lowered the year-ago comparison. A print at or above 2.0% lands the day before the policy decision and would move the residual doubt about that decision to zero, compressing the differential the pair depends on.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
catalysts.rationale: The only scheduled policy decision on either leg inside the tactical window, and it belongs to the quote currency. A 25bp move to 1.25% narrows the bilateral differential from 125bp to 100bp with no offsetting base-currency action available before 2026-10-28. Roughly 80-84% is priced, so the tradeable content is the pace language and the possibility of an outsized increase — both one-directional for this pair.

catalysts.event: US appropriations deadline and quote-economy interim fiscal half-year close
catalysts.rationale: Two coincident events that point the same way for this pair. A US government shutdown is precedented in 2026 and would be risk-negative, which hurts the base leg's pro-cyclical beta while adding a haven bid to the quote leg. Separately the quote economy's interim book-closing generates documented repatriation and dividend-related flows that are mechanically quote-currency positive.

catalysts.event: Base-economy Consumer Price Index for September
catalysts.rationale: The first base-economy CPI in which the gasoline base effect turns materially less favourable, and the first to capture tariff pass-through in both directions. Headline converging down toward the 2.0% core average removes the statistical support for the residual market-implied hike premium, which is the base currency's best remaining rate argument and therefore the pair's.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The first base-currency decision after the tactical window and the more consequential of the two late-October events for the base leg, because the bank must publish a full forecast round incorporating post-tariff activity data. Marking growth down for the tariff shock while marking inflation down as gasoline base effects roll off leaves the curve no basis for a 2026 hike, and removing that premium widens the compression already coming from the quote leg.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan decision with Outlook Report
catalysts.rationale: A projection round landing 48 hours after the base-currency one, and the pairing is the decisive communication event of the strategic window. The Board must revise forecasts into a terms-of-trade shock and a scheduled subsidy unwind, with its FY2027 core forecast already revised up and its objective reframed to prevent an upward inflation deviation. Two forecast rounds two days apart, both expected to resolve against the pair, is the densest catalyst cluster on the calendar.

The only dated circuit-breaker for the base economy's trade conflict inside the strategic horizon, and its own government expects no substantive talks before it — so a post-election negotiation restart is the clearest bullish scenario for the base leg. It also marks the point after which the US political incentive to support the quote currency weakens, since the joint intervention was publicly linked to domestic borrowing costs.

The final base-currency decision of 2026 and the terminal date for the market's residual year-end hike probability. If the bank has not moved by this meeting the entire premium comes out of the base-economy curve, worth an estimated 15-20bp on the two-year. Two of the six largest domestic banks forecast tightening by this date, so the meeting is a genuine binary for the base leg of the differential.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
catalysts.rationale: The second quote-currency hike is only lightly priced, with cumulative pricing implying roughly one move and no more inside 2026, while the published desk path has 1.50% arriving in January 2027 and analysts note a September move opens scope for a December squeeze-in toward quarterly tightening. A December delivery would take the bilateral differential to 75bp and would be a repricing rather than a confirmation.

catalysts.event: Japan FY2027 draft budget Cabinet approval
catalysts.rationale: Ministry requests total approximately JPY 143trn with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line at a 3.8% assumed rate. If new issuance breaches the stated cap, the quote economy's fiscal risk premium dominates its policy channel and higher Japanese yields become quote-currency-negative — the mechanism that has already produced benchmark Japanese bond yields breaking a three-decade barrier without a sustained currency rally. This is the single event most capable of killing the strategic bearish thesis from the quote side.

catalysts.event: US tariffs on base-economy cars, trucks, parts and steel rise to 50%
catalysts.rationale: A dated, pre-announced escalation extending the base economy's tariff exposure well beyond the current 5.2% of bilateral exports, striking the auto sector that drove its Q2 growth. Section 338 carries no expiry, so the escalation persists until a presidential proclamation removes it. It sits just beyond the strategic horizon but is the structural reason the base leg's event risk is scored bearish over one to six months.

assumptions: Price series as delivered: the payload supplied 130 weekday bars covering 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, with spot 112.96588 at spotDate 2026-09-03, zero weekend bars dropped, pip size 0.01. Moving averages, touch-counted zones, the 200-week figure and its slope, ATR(14), realised volatility and 52-week range statistics are computed over the whole stored history (2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03, 4,878 weekday bars), not just the 130 visible bars.

Information cut versus valuation date: the stated valuation date is 2026-09-01, but the payload's spotDate is 2026-09-03 — two days after it — and web evidence used extends to 2026-09-04. Every level, target, pip figure and distance-to-average is anchored to payload spot 112.96588 at 2026-09-03, using later information where material (the BoC hold delivered 2026-09-02 and the carry-trade unwind of 3-4 September). No fresher web spot has been substituted.

Spot basis conflict, disclosed not reconciled: the payload gives 112.96588 at 2026-09-03; the base-currency dossier carries a CAD/JPY cross of 115.149 dated 2026-08-28, which the payload's own daily series corroborates as that session's close (115.14854). The two are consistent once the two-session decline of 2-3 September is accounted for; the payload figure is used throughout.

Rates block vintage: ten-year yields in the payload are monthly observations as of 2026-06-01 on both legs (CAD 3.42%, JPY 2.67%, differential +75bp) and are never quoted as live levels. Dossier live prints (~3.74% and 2.94%, +79bp gap) are labelled as dossier-sourced and used for trajectory commentary only. Policy rates are live: CAD 2.25% as of 2026-08-31, JPY 1.00% as of 2026-09-01.

Implied volatility is an estimate, not a quote: CAD/JPY has no listed option. The store builds volatility from the variance identity using a realised correlation of 0.3408 standing in for an unobservable implied one, documented to run low (8.7% for EUR/GBP, 17.8% for EUR/CHF, 14.4% median across 17 pairs). Every carry-to-vol ratio derived from it is an upper bound; the longer-dated 7.743% is probably nearer 8.5-9% corrected. No risk reversal, IV percentile or barrier data exist for this cross.

Funding premium: the payload's −117.7bp annualised figure is a CME 6C/6J calendar-spread cross observed 2026-08-31 over a 14.6-to-49.6-day window. By covered interest parity it is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and the two cannot be separated without an OIS curve; the ~7bp residual against the +125bp policy differential is a derived attribution, not a quoted basis level. Forward outrights are model forwards, not dealer quotes.

No bank consensus for this pair: no bank research forecast for CAD/JPY as a pair could be sourced. The products that surface are extrapolation and audience-sentiment models, cited as such rather than presented as consensus; the derived National Bank cross of roughly 115 for end-2026 is explicitly a derivation from one desk's two separate legs.

Bilateral trade: figures are the supplied IMF DOTS goods series for 2024, cited directly and not re-estimated: base exports to quote US$10.9bn, base imports from quote US$16.2bn, net −US$5.2bn for the base economy. Bilateral services, FDI and portfolio flows are not in the payload; portfolio-flow context is web-sourced and labelled.

Weight adjustments: five adjustments applied, each within the ±0.05 limit: Factor 5 +0.04 tactical and +0.03 strategic, Factor 8 +0.01 strategic, Factor 10 −0.04 on both horizons. Both schedules sum to exactly 1.00.

Direction verdict provenance: all ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings and cross-horizon/consensus-divergence framing were scored in a first pass without the price payload and carried through unchanged. Net stances were derived mechanically from weighted scores against stated thresholds (−0.1027 clears −0.10 by 0.0027). Everything price-derived (market context, technicals, carry/forward arithmetic, entries, targets, stops, sizing, scenarios, path expectation, conviction ladders, risk/reward, invalidator levels, signpost thresholds) is second-pass work built on the payload.

Inherited caveats: the base dossier's REER percentile, volatility surface and touch-counted zones are cache-sourced and externally unverifiable; the quote dossier's IMF debt and deficit figures, sovereign ratings and 214.5% gross-debt measure are uncited; the quote economy's operative US auto tariff rate could not be established from a primary source and no rate is asserted.

Liquidity and execution: CAD/JPY is a second-tier cross executed in practice through its two dollar legs, with wider spreads than either leg against the dollar, no listed option, and demonstrated gap risk on official yen intervention — the payload's 30 April (357-pip range), 30 July (370-pip) and 3 September (227-pip) sessions all exceed 3x the 70-pip ATR(14). All position sizing reflects that.
